meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the R-201 unit
meta.scope: From the make-up gas battery limit (XV-202) round the synthesis loop: C-201, E-202, E-201, E-204, R-201 with its quench, E-203, V-201, the purge PV-203, blowdown HV-205 and PSV-201 to the let-down of crude methanol by LV-204; including the utilities (instrument air, cooling water, start-up steam, power).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Nitrogen, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
Front-end syngas compressor trip
XV-202 closed by a trip or spurious closure
FV-202 fails closed (instrument air)
N1.cons: Production stops; the loop keeps circulating and the beds cool until the reaction dies; loop pressure falls as the purge continues; restart needs the permissives

N1.dev: More make-up than the loop can convert
N1.causes:
FIC-202 SP raised (production push)
FT-202 reads low
FV-202 opened in MAN
N1.cons: More heat released in beds 1 and 2 → bed exits towards the catalyst limit; more purge and inerts
Lower production; beds cooler; purge falls

N1.causes: Reformer or shift upset: CO up, CO₂ down
N1.cons: Much more heat per kmol converted in beds 1 and 2: bed exits approach the trip; sintering; by-products

N1.causes: Reformer upset: CO down, CO₂ up
N1.cons: Less reaction heat, more water in the crude, production falls
Inerts build up; lower reactant partial pressure; purge rises; production and carbon efficiency fall

N1.causes:
Sulfur or chloride slip from the front end
Fe/Ni carbonyls from carbon steel in cold CO service
N1.cons: Top of bed 1 loses activity; heat release moves down; faster ageing; wax and hot spots from Fe/Ni deposits

N1.dev: Loop pressure driven up by the make-up
N1.causes:
Loop not consuming gas (reaction stopped) while make-up flows
front-end compressor at its maximum
N1.cons: Loop pressure rises towards the make-up pressure 86 bar g: flange leaks, rupture if relief fails

N1.dev: Loop gas back into the front end
N1.causes: Front-end pressure falls below the loop with FV-202 open and XV-202 still open
N1.cons: Loop depressures backwards; surge of the front-end compressor

N1.dev: XV-202 fails to close on demand
N1.causes: Stuck valve, solenoid failure: one final element serves every trip
N1.cons: Every trip that relies on stopping the make-up fails: runaway, overpressure or blow-by continue
All valves to fail positions: FV-202, PV-203, LV-204 shut; TV-211 and quench valves open → reaction dies, level rises slowly (see section 9)

recs.text: TSHH 2oo3: three elements per bed exit (TE-214A/B/C …) voted 2oo3, independent of the indication thermocouples.
XV-202B: second make-up shut-off valve in series (1oo2) so one stuck valve does not defeat every trip; proof-test both.
Make-up composition analyzer (CO, CO₂) with alarm and a written response to a reformer upset (cut FIC-202, raise quench margins).
Confirm PSV-201 relief cases (fire, blocked purge with make-up at maximum pressure, E-201/E-204 tube rupture) and car-seal the relief isolation valves.
Start-up procedure: admit make-up in MAN at ≤ 25 %, raise slowly while watching bed 1–2 exits; close E-204 steam and its block valve once self-sustaining; train on the simulator.
Verify on site that every valve goes to its fail position on instrument-air loss; keep XV-202 de-energise-to-trip.
Restart procedure after a trip: find the cause, reset only when the trip condition has cleared, reheat through E-204, then admit make-up per R22.
